summary: Quoting part of a conditional turns it into a string literal that is always truthy; ansible-core 2.19 reports it and the fix is to remove the stray quotes.
questions: Why is my assert always passing even when it should fail?
Why does quoting part of a when condition cause a 'must have a boolean result' error?
How do I combine 'is defined' and a length check correctly?

answer_card.title: Remove stray quotes inside a conditional
answer_card.answer_md:
Here the second half is quoted, so it is just a non-empty string and the assertion can never be false:

```yaml
- assert:
    that: inventory_hostname is defined and 'inventory_hostname | length > 0'
```

ansible-core 2.19 reports: `Conditional result was 'inventory_hostname | length > 0' of type 'str' ...`

Remove the quotes so it is evaluated as an expression:

```yaml
- assert:
    that: inventory_hostname is defined and inventory_hostname | length > 0
```
